text_blocks.snippet: Residents in Central Illinois are frequently targeted by common scams involving fake government text messages, impostor calls, online retail fraud, and tech support traps. Fraudsters frequently use artificial intelligence to mimic family members or officials, demanding urgent payments via untraceable methods.

list.snippet: Fake DMV / Secretary of State Texts: Scammers send text messages claiming your driver’s license or vehicle registration will be suspended unless you click a link to pay an overdue fee. The state never requests payment or personal data via text.
Impostor and AI Scams: Con artists pose as government agents, utility workers, or tech support, using fear and urgency to trick victims into sharing private login details or sending money.
Online Purchase & Pet Scams: Fake shopping sites or classified ads trap buyers looking for retail items or companion pets, taking money via peer-to-peer payment apps without delivering any goods.
Charity & Disaster Fraud: Phony organizations and callers solicit fake donations following emergency events or community tragedies.
Practice the pause: Take a step back when pressured to act immediately. Verify urgent requests by looking up official phone numbers independently.
Do not click links: Never open unsolicited links or attachments found in text messages or emails regarding tolls, traffic tickets, or package deliveries.
Guard your data: Never share banking details, passwords, or personal identification numbers over the phone with unknown contacts.

Report suspicious activity: Track and report fraudulent trends using resources like the Federal Trade Commission Fraud Reporting

portal or the local Better Business Bureau of Central Illinois.
